title: Review: the present tense
why: Review of the unit "The present tense": the four forms of regular verbs and short verbs, negation, יֵשׁ / אֵין, questions, and the modal verbs. You reuse all of it to describe your day, before moving on to everyday life.

The present tense at a glance

Four forms, depending on the gender and number of the subject, never on the person. So the pronoun is required, and a mixed group takes the masculine plural.

m. sg.f. sg.m. pl.f. pl.
כּוֹתֵב
kotev		כּוֹתֶבֶת
kotevet		כּוֹתְבִים
kotvim		כּוֹתְבוֹת
kotvot
שׁוֹתֶה
shote		שׁוֹתָה
shota		שׁוֹתִים
shotim		שׁוֹתוֹת
shotot
גָּר
gar		גָּרָה
gara		גָּרִים
garim		גָּרוֹת
garot
יָכוֹל
yakhol		יְכוֹלָה
yekhola		יְכוֹלִים
yekholim		יְכוֹלוֹת
yekholot

Three patterns to recognize: the o-e pattern (כּוֹתֵב, feminine in -et), verbs ending in ה (שׁוֹתֶה, רוֹצֶה, feminine in -a) and the short verbs (גָּר, קָם, בָּא, feminine in -a). יָכוֹל and צָרִיךְ are in a class of their own.

If you're a woman, all your sentences switch to the feminine: אֲנִי קָמָה, שׁוֹתָה, עוֹבֶדֶת. If you're a man: אֲנִי קָם, שׁוֹתֶה, עוֹבֵד.

", "

No, there is, questions

לֹא goes right before the verb or adjective. יֵשׁ (there is) and אֵין (there isn't) never change. For a question, you raise your voice, or put the question word first: מָה, מִי, אֵיפֹה, מָתַי, לָמָּה, אֵיךְ.

אֲנִי לֹא יָכוֹל לָבוֹא, כִּי אֲנִי עָסוּק.I can't come, because I'm busy. [ani lo yakhol lavo, ki ani asuk]
אֵין זְמַן!There's no time! [ein zman!]
מָתַי אַתֶּם אוֹכְלִים?When do you (pl.) eat? [matai atem okhlim?]

Adjectives like עָיֵף (tired) and עָסוּק (busy) also agree: אֲנִי עֲיֵפָה, I'm tired (a woman speaking). Still with no verb \"to be.\"

", "

Describing your day

With בַּבֹּקֶר (in the morning), בַּצָּהֳרַיִם (at noon), בָּעֶרֶב (in the evening), בַּלַּיְלָה (at night) and אַחַר כָּךְ (then, afterward), you can describe a whole day in the present. Here is Noa's:

כָּל יוֹם אֲנִי קָמָה מֻקְדָּם וְשׁוֹתָה קָפֶה.Every day, I get up early and drink a coffee. [kol yom ani kama mukdam ve-shota kafe]
בַּבֹּקֶר אֲנִי עוֹבֶדֶת, וּבַצָּהֳרַיִם אֲנִי אוֹכֶלֶת פִּתָּה.In the morning I work, and at noon I eat a pita. [ba-boker ani ovedet, u-va-tsohorayim ani okhelet pita]
אַחַר כָּךְ אֲנִי לוֹמֶדֶת עִבְרִית בָּאוּלְפָּן.Then I study Hebrew at the ulpan. [akhar kakh ani lomedet ivrit ba-ulpan]
בָּעֶרֶב אֲנִי אוֹהֶבֶת לִקְרֹא, אֲבָל בַּלַּיְלָה אֲנִי צְרִיכָה לִישֹׁן!In the evening I like to read, but at night I have to sleep! [ba-erev ani ohevet likro, aval ba-layla ani tsrikha lishon!]

Before ב, מ or פ, \"and\" is וּ (u): וּבַצָּהֳרַיִם, and at noon. Elsewhere, it's וְ (ve): וְשׁוֹתָה.
